newsitem.title: UK: Dollar sparkles, Euro bourses consolidate.
newsitem.headline: Dollar sparkles, Euro bourses consolidate.

text.p: The dollar sparkled in European trading on Monday, hitting a 42-month high above 114 yen against the generally weak Japanese currency, while key bourses largely consolidated Friday's revival.
A surprise takeover bid helped the London stock market, Europe's busiest, move back closer to recent record levels, and the Frankfurt bourse advanced more than one percent.
Paris, however, slipped back after a more positive start.

Market analysts said the yen suffered as Japanese investors kept on searching for higher-yielding investments abroad and amid uncertainty over the eventual political outcome after Japan's general election on October 20 left a hung parliament.
"Japanese investors are still showing a tremendous appetite for overseas assets," said Pat Magill, head of the corporate desk at Daiwa Europe in London.
"The political situation is uneasy at the moment and while that's going on, there's no chance of the Bank of Japan moving up (interest) rates," said economist David Bloom at HSBC James Capel.
Compared with its advance against the yen, the dollar showed less movement against the mark amid fading market hopes for German rate cuts.

Elsewhere, the pound scaled a 16-month peak of $1.6145, hit 2.4590 marks, its strongest against the German currency since December 1995, and touched 184.28 yen, its highest against the yen since February 1993. On a trade-weighted basis, the pound jumped to a two-and-a-half year high of 89.8 from Friday's close of 89.2.
U.S. stocks in London were mostly firmer on Monday and traders expected Wall Street to add to Friday's gains, when the Dow Jones industrial average rose 14.54 to 6,007.02.

But they said a busy week for U.S. data could prompt caution on markets focusing on the health of the American economy. A run of statistics will culminate in U.S. October jobs figures on Friday, although no key figures are due on Monday.

For those looking for advice, market guru Elaine Garzarelli, best known for forecasting the October 1987 Wall Street crash, repeated a prediction that the U.S. market could drop by between 15 percent and 25 percent by the end of this year.
However, the Frankfurt bourse shook off negative influences and gained ground as good corporate news boosted sentiment.
"This is not going to be a day for a furious advance but the phase of consolidation seems to have passed," said one dealer.
The London stock market quickly reversed slight opening losses to head higher after a boost from news of a surprise takeover bid for Northern Electric, whose shares rose 115 pence to 635 pence.
"We saw the bid lift the market," said one trader. "The market was going to be dull and drifting ahead of economic news this week but this has certainly lifted sentiment."

While London markets look ahead to the government budget in a month's time, this week's main economic diary entry in Britain is Wednesday's monthly monetary meeting between the finance minister and the governor of the Bank of England, although analysts expect no change in interest rates.
French shares began slightly higher, supported by the gains on Wall Street, but later lost momentum. Dealers said investors could show caution ahead of U.S. elections next week.
Lagardere fell more than five percent to 156.50 francs, after a good run in previous weeks, on growing unease about its planned takeover of Thomson.
CURRENCIES AT 1215 GMT
The dollar was trading around 1.5230 marks and 114.18 yen, compared with 1.5201 and 113.28 in late European business on Friday. It earlier hit a high of 114.30 yen.
STOCKS AT 1215 GMT
London's FTSE 100 index was up 12.0 points at 4,034.4.
Germany's DAX index was 31.03 ahead at 2,705.25.
In Paris the CAC-40 index was down 7.39 at 2,155.04.
Tokyo's Nikkei average gained 145.44 to 20,885.41 but brokers said investors were sidelined due to the unclear political situation.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1215 GMT
Gold was fixed at $382.80 an ounce in the morning and later traded around $383, compared with Friday's London close of $382.65. Silver edged up one cent to $4.93.
